standfirst: 49 STORIES · 7 REGIONS · EVERY ONE FROM SATURDAY 21 NOVEMBER 2026 (ANY TIME ZONE)
dateCheck: Left out on purpose: Thursday 19 and Friday 20 November, not Saturday’s news. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa’s first female deputy president, dies (20 Nov). Wall Street’s Friday close: S&P 500 and Dow in correction. Kryvyi Rih ballistic strike: 2 killed, including a 7-year-old, about 60 hurt. Equinor says the cyberattack has stopped (20 Nov). Haiti–El Salvador prisons deal (20 Nov). Depardieu/Houellebecq gang-rape probe (19–20 Nov). Morocco’s €366m defence-industry plan (18–20 Nov). A second judge blocks Trump’s DC memorial arch; Connecticut ICE-mask ruling; Iraq Jurf al-Nasr deal (Fri 20 Nov). European student and youth protests, including Berlin “GenZ regelt” (Fri 20 Nov). Japan closes EV subsidy applications early (Fri night). EU Council authorises signing of the Indonesia FTA (18 Nov). Long March-8A internet-satellite launch (20 Nov). Friday Russian objects in Polish airspace; Friday Jazan intercepts and Hodeidah strikes. Not yet: final COP31 text, Las Vegas GP race, ATP Finals final.
footer: Every story happened or was first reported on Saturday 21 November 2026 in some time zone. Claims stay attributed. Drawings are original. Sources include AFP, Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera, Kyodo, Yonhap, ABC, Dawn, IGP, Indeci, ESA.
offMap: Off the map: 37 Bitcoin · 38 triple star (no site named) · 46 BepiColombo at Mercury.
asteriskNote: * Saturday local time (still Friday UTC): Riyadh alert, Davao landing, Tochigi train.
sure: HOW SURE: OFFICIAL on the record · CONFIRMED wires agree · REPORTED one outlet or figures differ · CLAIM one side only.

stories.headline: COP31 runs into overtime
stories.dek: No cover decision yet. Third draft is due today.

stories.headline: Riyadh: 3 missiles downed*
stories.dek: Three missiles downed, then a drone in the south.

stories.headline: Peru M6.7, no deaths reported
stories.dek: Depth 129 km. One hurt in Lima. No tsunami alert.

stories.headline: Rutte stands with Poland
stories.dek: Allies stand with Poland after talks. No Article 4.

stories.text: Podil: ballistic missile hit about 05:47 local; two houses burned, one person hurt.

stories.headline: Killer-robot talks fail
stories.dek: No binding mandate. Rules talks run to 2028.

stories.text: Act VI: sixth Saturday of cost-of-living marches; about 70,000 police. Turnout falling.
Gaza City: Palestinian media report 3 killed in an Israeli airstrike.
IRGC claims it downed a US MQ-9 over Hormuz (“58th”). No US confirmation.
Hormuz still restricted: 6 AIS-visible commercial crossings, about 9% of normal.

stories.headline: PX19: all 146 safe*
stories.dek: Fire warning, then a Davao slide. All 146 safe.

stories.headline: India 486-4, lead 118
stories.dek: Rahul makes 136, his 13th ton. Gill falls for 98.

stories.text: Cricket Australia unanimously backs Pat Cummins as Test captain.
Fukushima: over 1,000 cut off in Urabandai, Kitashiobara, by snow and fallen trees.
Osaka: BTS win five MAMA awards. Cortis take Song of the Year.
Five freight-train cars derail near Sejong; Saemaeul and Mugunghwa services stop.
Lee visits an Ulsan AI data-centre site and repeats the ₩100m CSAT-cheating reward.
Seoul: a bus rams the pavement near Hongik Univ. Station, injuring 6.
Kyushu basho: Onosato and Wakamotoharu go into the final day tied at 12-2.
Princess Aiko returns home from her Singapore visit, 60 years of ties.
Seoul: Choi Min-jeong wins a third straight World Tour 1,000m title.
University essay and interview exams begin across South Korea (21–22 Nov).

stories.headline: Garment unrest shuts mills
stories.dek: 50–80 mills in Savar and Ashulia stop work.

stories.text: PCB central contracts for 38 players leave out Rizwan, Shan Masood and Saim Ayub.
India SCO forum: Pakistan’s climate minister calls climate change the “enemy” of civilisations.
Kenya: a party seeks court orders against the IEBC CEO appointment.
Nigeria: Peter Obi vows to end kidnappings and corruption.
South Africa: Premium Times reports nearly 600 women killed in three months.
Eswatini: dirty foam prompts a Ngwempisi River pollution probe.
African Group at COP31: “we came to claim what is rightfully ours”; $120bn adaptation ask.

stories.headline: Verstappen on pole
stories.dek: Pole, then a five-place penalty. Race not run.

stories.text: Florida: St. Johns near Cocoa at 18.76 ft, major flood. Rockledge told to be ready to leave.
Spaniards abroad start voting for the 29 Nov election; 500k+ eligible in Argentina.
Bitcoin about $58,460, down about 5% in 24 hours (reference price, 12:30 UTC).
Astronomers find a nearby “weirdo” triple-star system. No site named.
Dozens of rallies over midwife-supported homebirth and insurance rules.
Gold Coast Schoolies week begins, with numbers down.
Four people struck by lightning at the Strawberry Fields festival, Tocumwal.
Sydney: two teens stabbed at a shopping centre; a 17-year-old is charged.
Japan’s ministry weighs ISP blocking after the GMO breach.
Kunio Tashima stays in the FIFA presidential race.
Tochigi*: an express train hits a stalled car. All 300 passengers unhurt.

stories.headline: BepiColombo at Mercury
stories.dek: Enters orbit. Insertion burn from 18:24 UTC.

stories.text: Turin: Alcaraz beats Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6(1) to reach Sunday’s final.
PL: Man City 1-1 Fulham (Haaland goal ruled out); Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal; Chelsea 1-4 Leeds.

stories.headline: England 37-12 All Blacks
stories.dek: Record England win over New Zealand.
